disposition_mapping.rationale: Extraction becomes system-driven with exception-based human oversight, but the risk-rated schedule and closing exchange rates remain mandatory consumed inputs, preserving ACR-R-01, ACR-R-07 and the KB-07 FX retranslation requirement.
Matching is restructured around an automated engine with accountant triage of residual exceptions, satisfying ACR-R-02's requirement that transaction matching survive while increasing throughput.
Investigation and classification remains a human judgment activity performed by the GL accountant, unchanged in substance per ACR-R-03 and KB-02's requirement for an evidential trail.

Adjusting journal entry preparation is merged with the (unconstrained) preparer sign-off into one preparer step; the prior-period error record remains a mandatory input, satisfying ACR-R-04, ACR-R-06 and KB-05's error-correction principle.

Preparer sign-off is unconstrained by design and is absorbed into the journal preparation/submission act, since a separate attestation gate added no distinct control once the preparer's action itself is logged; independent review remains a separate actor in TS-05, preserving ACR-R-05.

Reviewer approval survives as an independent control performed by the finance controller, now merged with aged-item escalation into a single review cycle, satisfying ACR-R-09 and the actor-separation requirement ACR-R-05 against TS-04.

Escalation of aged reconciling items is unconstrained by design and is folded into the reviewer's approval step so aged items are flagged at the point of review rather than in a separate downstream pass.
Evidence retention and status reporting survive, now automated via an evidence repository and dashboard reporting, preserving the KB-02 evidential trail and satisfying ACR-R-08.

steps.description: An extraction engine automatically pulls GL and comparison balances (bank, subledger, third-party) for every in-scope account per its risk-rated schedule, retranslating foreign-currency balances at the closing rate. The GL accountant reviews only flagged extraction exceptions rather than performing manual pulls.
inputs: Reconciliation schedule by account risk rating
steps.name: Automated balance extraction and FX retranslation

steps.description: A rules- and pattern-based matching engine auto-matches the majority of transactions between the GL and comparison source; the GL accountant triages and manually resolves the residual unmatched population.
steps.name: Automated transaction matching with exception triage

steps.description: Unmatched items are investigated, explained, supported with evidence and classified by the GL accountant, with system-suggested root causes accelerating investigation.
steps.name: Investigate and classify reconciling items

steps.description: The GL accountant prepares adjusting journal entries for items requiring correction, correcting prior-period errors retrospectively, and submits the completed reconciliation package in a single accountable preparer action that supersedes the former standalone sign-off step.
steps.name: Prepare adjusting journal entries and submit reconciliation

steps.description: An independent finance controller reviews and approves the reconciliation and its adjusting entries, and in the same review cycle escalates any reconciling items beyond the ageing threshold for resolution, eliminating a separate downstream escalation pass.
steps.name: Reviewer approval with integrated aged-item escalation

steps.description: Reconciliation evidence is automatically captured in the evidence repository and reconciliation status is reported to stakeholders and governance dashboards, preserving the evidential trail linking journals and reconciliations to reported balances.
steps.name: Retain evidence and report reconciliation status
